keyFindings.description:
makesTable (line 68) treats a header line longer than maxTableHeaderRead (4 KiB) as making a table, so a title line feed before a delimiter row is written 
 where main writes it raw and both readers hold main's bytes (header and delimiter row of different widths). Reproduced at d0cc0875: 'p | q | ' + 5000 x + ' ![a](i "a\n|-|\nb")' renders 'a
|-|
b'; with 10 x it keeps the raw bytes. This is churn that acceptance (3) forbids, and the differential and the generated test do not see it because no corpus has a header line over 4 KiB. Fix in linear time without the byte cap, or the architect records it as an accepted exception to (3) and the PR body names it; add a corpus case either way.

After a row is refused as strips-link (line 430), the live document never gets its structs, so every later row from the same client has a clock gap, parks, and sets rebuiltAt; pendingNotice (connection.ts:23) checks rebuiltAt first, so the user is told 'the document was rebuilt since' and the link notice never shows whenever the old editor wrote more than one row after the strip. The pending-sync test covers one row only. Attribute later parks from a client whose row was refused as strips-link to strippedAt, and add a two-row test.
